context.synopsis: On January 27, 2025, President Trump removed NLRB member Gwynne Wilcox and fired two Democratic EEOC commissioners, Charlotte Burrows and Jocelyn Samuels. The removals left both independent bodies without the quorum required for some commission- or board-level decisions. The NLRB's regional enforcement work continued, but the Board could not issue decisions without a quorum.
context.recovered_rationale: This matters because removing the sitting boards left the labor and anti-discrimination agencies below the quorum needed for official action. The documented consequence was paralysis in prosecuting unfair labor practices, certifying union elections, and pursuing systemic discrimination cases. Conflicting court views and organizational lawsuits also raised a significant concern about the legality of removing protected independent-agency officials.

correction.original_claim_summary: Trump allegedly fired all NLRB and EEOC board members on January 27, 2025, paralyzing both agencies.

identified_problems.explanation: Trump did not fire all members of either body. He removed NLRB member Gwynne Wilcox and NLRB General Counsel Jennifer Abruzzo, and fired two Democratic EEOC commissioners, Charlotte Burrows and Jocelyn Samuels.
Loss of quorum prevented the NLRB Board and EEOC Commission from taking certain board-level actions, but did not eliminate all agency enforcement work.
